The other chapter headings in this set use arabic numerals (p.44 'CAPVT 3.', p.50 'CAP. 4.', p.51 'CAPVT 5.'), so arabic 1 is the probable reading.

verdicts.my_reading: quadrante : quandoquidem licet monàs

decisions.seen: At 8x a clear grave accent (stroke running from upper left to lower right) sits over the a of 'monàs'.

verdicts.note: The print has a space before the colon in 'quadrante :' (convention). The line is 14th only if the diagram above is not counted.

verdicts.my_reading: tonium,quod Díeſi duplo acutius eſt: Po-

decisions.seen: The line clearly begins with bold-inked 'to' before 'nium', carrying on from 'hemito-' at the end of the line above. Reading 2 drops 'to'.
No space after the comma ('tonium,quod' is tight). This is only spacing after punctuation.

verdicts.my_reading: diametro , dimidium dati quadrati habe-

decisions.seen: The third letter of the word has a crossbar at x-height and a curved foot hooking right below the baseline: a t, like the t in 'metro' on the same line. The r in 'metro' has a flat symmetrical base serif instead. The word is 'dati'.

verdicts.note: The print has a space before the comma in 'diametro ,' (convention).

verdicts.my_reading: re datum. Sedecim nanq; numerum qua-

decisions.seen: At 6x the word is printed 'nanq;'. The third letter has two stems (an n, not the three stems of an m), followed by q with the semicolon-shaped que abbreviation. Expanded, it reads 'nanque'.

verdicts.my_reading: paſôn nnncupata : ſed hæc non ſine me-

decisions.seen: At 6x the second letter is closed at the top (an arch joining both stems) and open at the bottom, the same shape as an n. It is probably a turned u. The print therefore shows the misprint 'nnncupata'; reading 2 reproduces it.

verdicts.note: The print has a space before the colon in 'nnncupata :' (convention).

verdicts.my_reading: ſteríora interualla vocantur.

decisions.seen: Over the first i of 'ſteriora' there is an elongated slanted mark, heavy at the lower left with a thin tail rising to the upper right: an acute. It is about twice the width of the round dot over the i of 'interualla' on the same line.

verdicts.my_reading: uenit tempor(is) ſpacio, acuto cùm graui

decisions.seen: A small, lightly inked mark (about 5 px, mid-dark ink) sits over the right half of the u of 'cum', sloping down to the right (grave direction). It is separated by a clear gap from the q-descender of 'æquo' in the line above. It is smaller and fainter than the grave on 'verò' in the line above, but it is distinct ink, not paper texture.

verdicts.note: In 'temporis' the final 'is' seems to be set in a different (italic-looking) sort. This cannot be shown in a plain transcription.

verdicts.my_reading: neturq́ue. Dià-paſôn autem per octo di-

decisions.seen: In the darkness map the acute stands over the bowl of the q (columns of the q), not over the u. The u before r and the u after q carry no accent. The print is 'neturq́ue', so 'netúrque' wrongly puts an accent on u.
The same point: the accent is on the q (q-acute sort), and a full stop follows 'que'. Reading 2's ú is not printed.

verdicts.my_reading: paſson cum Dià-pénte, triplex : Bis Dià-

decisions.seen: At 7x the word is a tall long-s followed by a short round s ('paſson'), so 'passon'. There is no circumflex on the o.
There is a visible space between 'triplex' and the colon. Reading 1 matches the print's spacing, but this is only spacing before punctuation.

verdicts.my_reading: CAP. 4.

decisions.seen: The heading is letterspaced small caps 'C A P.' with a full stop after P, then '4.'. No VT is printed.

verdicts.my_reading: datum vel longitudine vel craſſitudine:

decisions.seen: The third letter has a faint pointed stem tip rising above x-height, an arm to the right at x-height, and a foot that runs off to the right at the baseline. That makes it a t. The r of 'rum' in line 10 has no ascender and a symmetrical base serif. The print reads 'chor-datum', a misprint for 'chordarum', reproduced as printed.

verdicts.my_reading: runtur , neque hemitoniis omnino,neque

decisions.seen: There is a clear space between 'runtur' and the comma (as in reading 2), but this is only spacing before punctuation.

The comma sits tight after 'omnino' with no space (spacing convention). The first letter of the second 'neque' is weakly inked: two stems joined by a thin arch at the top, visible on tone stretch, i.e. a damaged n. No dot is printed under it. Reading 2's underdot is an editorial sign of uncertainty; the letter is n, as in reading 1.

verdicts.my_reading: ſáron genus Chromáticum , ex Hemito-

decisions.seen: In the darkness map an acute stroke rises from lower left to upper right directly over the a after m. The dot of the following i is separate and round.
There is a space between 'Chromáticum' and the comma, but this is only spacing before punctuation.

verdicts.my_reading: vero per duas dieſes modulatio peraga-

decisions.seen: No inked accent is over the o of 'vero'. At very high tone stretch only a diffuse grey blotch shows above the left of the o, at the same level as the paper mottling nearby. Compare the crisp black grave on 'verò' in line 9 of the same page.

verdicts.my_reading: tur, quòd ſit optimum , ab ipſa communi

decisions.seen: At 7x a clear grave (upper left to lower right) sits over the o of 'quòd'.
There is a space between 'optimum' and the comma, but this is only spacing before punctuation.

result.summary: I decided all 17 places from enlarged crops and pixel darkness maps of the page images. Main results: (1) The q-acute sort ('q́ue') appears at 41.15 (ipſaq́ue) and 47.7 (neturq́ue.). Reading 1 at 41.15 moves the accent onto the a and reading 2 at 47.7 moves it onto the u; neither placement is printed. (2) Misprints reproduced as printed: 'nnncupata' (46.13) and, with medium confidence, 'chor-datum' (50.5); the t has a short ascender and a right-turning foot. (3) Three accents are faint or absent: cùm at 47.27 is a small faint grave, judged present (medium); vero at 52.15 has no inked accent (medium); steríora at 47.14 is a clear acute. (4) CAPVT 1 vs I at 41.3: the glyph has the same shape as the old-style arabic 1 in the page number. Because the other chapter headings use arabic numerals, I chose '1' (medium). Five places differ only in spacing around punctuation and are marked convention. My crops are in scratchpad/wf4/vinet-B/.
